sections.title: Comparing two groups: the coefficient of variation as referee

board_events.text: Which group is steadier?
A coach, a buyer, an investor — all ask the same practical question: which one is more consistent?
If σ alone: a ₹5 spread on a ₹50 mean is a very different wobble from ₹5 on a ₹5000 mean.
Measure spread RELATIVE to size: divide σ by the mean, times 100.

board_events.text: Being a pure ratio, C.V. compares any two series — rupees vs runs. Lower C.V. = more consistent.

segments.text: The final subtopic answers the most practical question in the chapter: how do you compare the spread of two different groups?
A coach choosing between two batsmen, a buyer comparing two brands, an investor weighing two funds, they're all asking the same thing, which one is steadier?

Standard deviation alone can't always referee this. A spread of five rupees around a mean of fifty is a huge relative wobble, but a spread of five rupees around a mean of five thousand is almost nothing. Same sigma, completely different meaning.
So the fix is to measure spread relative to the size of what you're measuring. Divide the standard deviation by the mean, and multiply by one hundred to get a percentage.
That is the coefficient of variation: sigma over x bar, times one hundred. One clean percentage that captures relative spread.

The picture makes it visual. On the top bar, a sigma of five sits on a mean of forty, that's a big relative wobble, a high coefficient of variation. On the bottom bar, the very same sigma of five sits on a mean of two hundred, and it's a tiny relative wobble, a low coefficient of variation.

Because it's a pure ratio with no units, the coefficient of variation compares any two series at all, rupees against runs, heights against marks. And the rule stays friendly: lower coefficient of variation means more consistent.
Aakhri subtopic chapter ka sabse practical sawaal answer karta hai: aap do alag groups ki spread kaise compare karte ho?
Ek coach do batsmen mein se chunta hua, ek buyer do brands compare karta hua, ek investor do funds tolta hua, sab ek hi cheez poochh rahe hain, kaunsa zyada steady hai?

Standard deviation akela hamesha ye referee nahi kar sakta. Pachaas ke mean ke aas-paas paanch rupee ki spread ek huge relative wobble hai, par paanch hazaar ke mean ke aas-paas paanch rupee ki spread lagbhag kuch bhi nahi. Same sigma, bilkul alag matlab.
Toh fix hai spread ko us cheez ke size ke relative measure karna jise aap naap rahe ho. Standard deviation ko mean se divide karo, aur one hundred se multiply karke percentage nikaalo.
Yahi coefficient of variation hai: sigma over x bar, times one hundred. Ek clean percentage jo relative spread pakadta hai.

Picture ise visual bana deta hai. Upar wale bar pe, paanch ki sigma chalis ke mean pe baithi hai, ye ek big relative wobble hai, ek high coefficient of variation. Neeche wale bar pe, wahi paanch ki sigma do sau ke mean pe baithi hai, aur ye ek tiny relative wobble hai, ek low coefficient of variation.

Kyunki ye ek pure ratio hai bina units ke, coefficient of variation kisi bhi do series ko compare karta hai, rupees ko runs se, heights ko marks se. Aur rule friendly rehta hai: kam coefficient of variation matlab zyada consistent.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Same mean or different mean: which comparison to use

board_events.text: Pick the right tool for the comparison
Same mean? The answer is easy — just compare σ directly; the smaller σ is steadier.
Different means (or different units)? σ alone can't referee — you MUST use C.V.
When means are equal, C.V. and σ give the SAME ranking — so σ is enough.
So the extra work of C.V. only earns its keep when the means differ.
The classic exam trap: comparing different-mean series by σ instead of C.V.

segments.text: Before you reach for the coefficient of variation on every problem, learn when it's actually needed, because sometimes it's overkill.
If the two groups have the same mean, the comparison is easy. Just compare their standard deviations directly, and the smaller sigma is the steadier group. No division needed.
But if the two groups have different means, or worse, different units, standard deviation alone cannot referee the contest. Here you must use the coefficient of variation.

Here's the key logical point, and examiners test it. When the means are equal, the coefficient of variation and the standard deviation give exactly the same ranking, because dividing both by the same mean can't change the order.
So the extra step of computing the coefficient of variation only earns its keep when the means genuinely differ. On equal means, it's just wasted arithmetic.
You can write the rule cleanly: if x bar one equals x bar two, compare sigma directly. Otherwise, go to the coefficient of variation.

<whisper>And here's the classic exam trap in this subtopic: comparing two series with different means by their standard deviations. A larger sigma does not mean more variable if the means differ. Normalise first.
Har problem pe coefficient of variation uthaane se pehle, seekho ki ye kab actually zaroori hai, kyunki kabhi kabhi ye overkill hai.
Agar do groups ka mean same hai, comparison aasaan hai. Bas unki standard deviations seedhe compare karo, aur chhoti sigma steadier group hai. Koi division nahi chahiye.
Lekin agar do groups ke means alag hain, ya usse bhi bura, alag units, toh standard deviation akela muqabla referee nahi kar sakta. Yahaan aapko coefficient of variation use karna hi padega.

Yahaan key logical point hai, aur examiners ise test karte hain. Jab means barabar hain, coefficient of variation aur standard deviation exactly same ranking dete hain, kyunki dono ko same mean se divide karna order nahi badal sakta.
Toh coefficient of variation compute karne ka extra step tabhi apni jagah banata hai jab means genuinely alag hon. Barabar means pe, ye bas wasted arithmetic hai.
Rule saaf likha ja sakta hai: agar x bar one equals x bar two, sigma seedhe compare karo. Warna, coefficient of variation pe jao.

<whisper>Aur yahaan is subtopic ka classic exam trap hai: do series jinke means alag hain unhe standard deviations se compare karna. Badi sigma ka matlab zyada variable nahi hai agar means alag hon. Pehle normalise karo.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Running the machinery backwards: the two master totals

board_events.text: The engine behind every reverse problem
A second family of problems runs the machinery backwards: given the mean and variance, reconstruct data.
The mean is built from ∑x_i; the variance from ∑x_i². Track those two totals and you can solve almost anything.
Every missing-observation and correction question is just bookkeeping on these two numbers.
Two unknowns need two constraints — the mean and the variance supply exactly that.

segments.text: This subtopic is famous for a second family of problems, and they run the whole machinery backwards.
Instead of here is the data, find the variance, they ask the reverse: here is the mean and the variance, now reconstruct the missing data, or repair a value that was recorded wrongly.

The insight that cracks them all is this: the mean is built entirely from the sum of the x i, and the variance is built from the sum of the x i squared. If you can track how those two running totals change, you can solve almost anything.
The first master total comes straight from the mean. Since x bar is the sum of x i over n, the sum of x i must equal n times x bar. That converts a given mean into a hard number.

The second comes from the shortcut variance. Since sigma squared is the sum of x i squared over n, minus x bar squared, rearranging gives the sum of x i squared equals n times the quantity sigma squared plus x bar squared.
So every missing-observation problem and every correction problem is really just bookkeeping on these two numbers, the sum of the values and the sum of their squares.
And there's a clean reason they work. Two unknowns always need two independent constraints to pin them down, and the mean plus the variance supply exactly two.
Ye subtopic ek doosre family of problems ke liye famous hai, aur wo poori machinery ko ulta chalate hain.
Yahaan data hai, variance nikaalo ke bajaye, wo ulta poochhte hain: yahaan mean aur variance hai, ab missing data reconstruct karo, ya ek value repair karo jo galat record hui thi.

Insight jo in sabko crack karti hai wo ye hai: mean poori tarah sum of the x i se banta hai, aur variance sum of the x i squared se. Agar aap track kar sako ki wo do running totals kaise badalte hain, aap lagbhag kuch bhi solve kar sakte ho.
Pehla master total seedhe mean se aata hai. Kyunki x bar sum of x i over n hai, sum of x i n times x bar ke barabar hona chahiye. Ye ek diye gaye mean ko ek hard number mein badal deta hai.

Doosra shortcut variance se aata hai. Kyunki sigma squared sum of x i squared over n hai, minus x bar squared, rearrange karne pe milta hai sum of x i squared equals n times the quantity sigma squared plus x bar squared.
Toh har missing-observation problem aur har correction problem asal mein sirf in do numbers pe bookkeeping hai, values ka sum aur unke squares ka sum.
Aur inke kaam karne ki ek clean wajah hai. Do unknowns ko pin karne ke liye hamesha do independent constraints chahiye, aur mean plus variance exactly do dete hain.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: When the coefficient of variation breaks down

board_events.text: The fine print on C.V.
C.V. needs a non-zero mean (x̄ ≠ 0); it is undefined otherwise and unstable near zero.
It is meant for ratio data with a true zero — heights, wages, marks.
Applying C.V. to °C (where zero is arbitrary) gives nonsense.
“More consistent” (lower C.V.) is NOT the same as “better.”
A consistent low scorer is still a low scorer — always read what the question rewards.
So: use C.V. for relative spread, but answer the question actually asked.

segments.text: The coefficient of variation is powerful, but it comes with fine print you must respect, or you'll apply it where it makes no sense.

First, it needs a non-zero mean. Since you're dividing by x bar, the coefficient of variation is simply undefined when the mean is zero, and it becomes wildly unstable and misleading when the mean is close to zero.
Second, it's meant for ratio data, data with a genuine, true zero. Heights, wages, and marks all qualify, because zero of each means a real absence of the quantity.

But apply it to something like temperature in degrees Celsius, where the zero is arbitrary, not a true absence of heat, and the coefficient of variation gives complete nonsense. The scale's zero has to mean something.
Third, and this one trips up strong students: more consistent, meaning a lower coefficient of variation, is not the same as better.
A consistent low scorer is still a low scorer. Consistency measures steadiness, not quality, so always read carefully what the question is actually rewarding.

So the balanced habit is this: reach for the coefficient of variation to judge relative spread, but then answer the question that was actually asked, consistency and performance are different verdicts.
Coefficient of variation powerful hai, par ye fine print ke saath aata hai jise aapko respect karna hoga, warna aap use wahaan apply karoge jahaan iska koi matlab nahi.

Pehla, ise ek non-zero mean chahiye. Kyunki aap x bar se divide kar rahe ho, coefficient of variation simply undefined hai jab mean zero ho, aur ye wildly unstable aur misleading ho jaata hai jab mean zero ke paas ho.
Doosra, ye ratio data ke liye hai, aisa data jiska ek genuine, true zero ho. Heights, wages, aur marks sab qualify karte hain, kyunki inme se har ek ka zero quantity ki ek real absence hai.

Lekin ise kisi cheez pe apply karo jaise temperature in degrees Celsius, jahaan zero arbitrary hai, garmi ki true absence nahi, aur coefficient of variation complete nonsense deta hai. Scale ke zero ka kuch matlab hona chahiye.
Teesra, aur ye strong students ko phasa deta hai: zyada consistent, matlab kam coefficient of variation, better hone ke barabar nahi hai.
Ek consistent low scorer phir bhi ek low scorer hai. Consistency steadiness naapti hai, quality nahi, toh hamesha dhyan se padho ki question actually kya reward kar raha hai.

Toh balanced aadat ye hai: relative spread judge karne ke liye coefficient of variation uthao, par phir wo question answer karo jo actually poochha gaya, consistency aur performance alag verdicts hain.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Procedure: comparing two distributions for consistency

board_events.text: A clean three-step comparison
Step 1: compute x̄ and σ for each series.
Step 2: if the means are equal, compare σ directly.
Step 3: the smaller C.V. is more consistent/stable; the larger C.V. is more variable.
Why divide by the mean: it converts an absolute wobble into a relative one — a fair comparison across scales.
Reverse form, if C.V. and σ are given: x̄ = (σ / C.V.) × 100.

segments.text: Let's turn all that intuition into a clean, repeatable procedure for comparing two distributions.
Step one, compute both summary numbers for each series, the mean x bar and the standard deviation sigma. You need both before you can decide anything.
Step two, check the means. If the two means are equal, you can compare the standard deviations directly and you're done, no coefficient of variation needed.
Otherwise, when the means differ, compute the coefficient of variation for each series: sigma over x bar, times one hundred. That's the fair yardstick when the scales differ.
Step three, read the verdict. The series with the smaller coefficient of variation is more consistent and stable; the larger one is more variable.
Always know why you're dividing by the mean: it converts an absolute wobble into a relative one, which is what makes the comparison fair across different scales in the first place.

And keep one algebraic cousin handy for reverse problems. If a question gives you the coefficient of variation and the standard deviation, you can recover the mean: x bar equals sigma over the coefficient of variation, times one hundred.
Chalo us saari intuition ko ek clean, repeatable procedure mein badalte hain do distributions compare karne ke liye.
Step one, har series ke liye dono summary numbers compute karo, mean x bar aur standard deviation sigma. Kuch bhi decide karne se pehle aapko dono chahiye.
Step two, means check karo. Agar do means barabar hain, aap standard deviations seedhe compare kar sakte ho aur kaam khatam, koi coefficient of variation nahi chahiye.
Warna, jab means alag hon, har series ke liye coefficient of variation compute karo: sigma over x bar, times one hundred. Jab scales alag hon toh yahi fair yardstick hai.
Step three, verdict padho. Jis series ka coefficient of variation chhota hai wo zyada consistent aur stable hai; bada wala zyada variable hai.
Hamesha jaano ki aap mean se kyun divide kar rahe ho: ye ek absolute wobble ko relative mein badalta hai, jo pehli jagah pe comparison ko alag scales pe fair banata hai.

Aur reverse problems ke liye ek algebraic cousin handy rakho. Agar ek question aapko coefficient of variation aur standard deviation deta hai, aap mean recover kar sakte ho: x bar equals sigma over the coefficient of variation, times one hundred.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Procedure: finding missing observations from mean and variance

board_events.text: Two unknowns, two equations
Step 1: turn the mean into ∑x_i = nx̄ — one equation in the unknowns.
Step 2: turn the variance into ∑(x_i − x̄)² = nσ² — a second equation.
Step 3: solve the two simultaneously.
From p+q (known) and p²+q² (known), the identity hands you the product pq — then roots of t²−(p+q)t+pq=0.
Two unknowns need two independent constraints; mean + variance are exactly those two.

segments.text: Now the procedure for the most popular JEE Main reverse problem, finding missing observations when you're told the mean and the variance.

Step one, translate the given mean into the first master total. The sum of x i equals n times x bar. With three known values and two unknowns, this gives you one equation, the unknowns sum to a fixed number.

Step two, translate the given variance. The sum of squared deviations, x i minus x bar all squared, equals n times sigma squared. Subtract off the known observations' contributions, and you get a second equation in the two unknowns.
Step three, solve the two equations simultaneously. You now know the sum of the two unknowns and the sum of their squared deviations, which is enough to pin them both down.
The neat shortcut uses the algebraic identity: p plus q, all squared, equals p squared plus q squared, plus two p q. You already know p plus q and p squared plus q squared.
So the identity hands you the product p q directly. With the sum and the product in hand, p and q are just the roots of a quadratic, t squared minus the sum times t, plus the product, equals zero.
The reason this always closes is the same as before: two unknowns need two independent constraints, and the mean and the variance are exactly those two constraints.
Ab sabse popular JEE Main reverse problem ka procedure, missing observations dhoondhna jab aapko mean aur variance bataye jaayein.

Step one, diye gaye mean ko pehle master total mein translate karo. Sum of x i equals n times x bar. Teen known values aur do unknowns ke saath, ye aapko ek equation deta hai, unknowns ka sum ek fixed number hai.

Step two, diye gaye variance ko translate karo. Sum of squared deviations, x i minus x bar poora squared, equals n times sigma squared. Known observations ke contributions ghata do, aur aapko do unknowns mein ek doosra equation milta hai.
Step three, dono equations ko simultaneously solve karo. Ab aap do unknowns ka sum aur unke squared deviations ka sum jaante ho, jo dono ko pin karne ke liye kaafi hai.
Neat shortcut ek algebraic identity use karta hai: p plus q, poora squared, equals p squared plus q squared, plus two p q. Aap pehle se p plus q aur p squared plus q squared jaante ho.
Toh identity aapko product p q seedhe de deti hai. Sum aur product haath mein hote hi, p aur q bas ek quadratic ke roots hain, t squared minus the sum times t, plus the product, equals zero.
Iske hamesha band hone ki wajah wahi hai jo pehle thi: do unknowns ko do independent constraints chahiye, aur mean aur variance theek wahi do constraints hain.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Procedure: correcting a misrecorded observation

board_events.text: Repair BOTH totals, not just the mean
Step 1: recover the wrong totals — ∑x = nx̄ and ∑x² = n(σ² + x̄²).
Step 3: recompute x̄ and σ from the repaired totals.
A wrong value pollutes BOTH ∑x (the mean) and ∑x² (the variance) — clean both.
If the value was omitted (not replaced): drop −w and −w² only, and reduce n by 1.

segments.text: The last procedure repairs a data set after a value was recorded wrongly, and the whole art is in remembering to clean two totals, not one.

Step one, recover the wrong totals from the reported statistics. The wrong sum of x is n times the wrong mean, and the wrong sum of x squared is n times the quantity wrong variance plus wrong mean squared.

Step two for the sum: subtract the wrong value's contribution and add the correct one's. The corrected sum of x equals the wrong sum, minus w, plus c, where w is the wrong value and c is the correct value.
Step two for the sum of squares: do the identical repair but with squares. The corrected sum of x squared equals the wrong sum of squares, minus w squared, plus c squared.
Step three, recompute the mean and standard deviation from the two repaired totals, and you have your corrected answers.

Here is the reasoning that stops students losing half the marks: a single wrong value polluted both the sum of x, which drives the mean, and the sum of x squared, which drives the variance. You must clean both, fixing only the mean is the most common half-mark loss.
One variation to watch. If the value was omitted entirely rather than replaced, you drop only the minus w and minus w squared, and you reduce n by one, since there's one fewer observation.
Aakhri procedure ek data set ko repair karta hai jab ek value galat record hui thi, aur poori kala do totals clean karna yaad rakhne mein hai, ek nahi.
Step one, reported statistics se wrong totals recover karo. Wrong sum of x n times the wrong mean hai, aur wrong sum of x squared n times the quantity wrong variance plus wrong mean squared hai.
Sum ke liye step two: wrong value ka contribution ghatao aur correct wala jodo. Corrected sum of x equals the wrong sum, minus w, plus c, jahaan w wrong value hai aur c correct value.
Sum of squares ke liye step two: bilkul wahi repair karo par squares ke saath. Corrected sum of x squared equals the wrong sum of squares, minus w squared, plus c squared.
Step three, do repaired totals se mean aur standard deviation dobara compute karo, aur aapke paas aapke corrected answers hain.

Yahaan wo reasoning hai jo students ko aadhe marks khone se rokti hai: ek akeli wrong value ne dono ko pollute kiya, sum of x, jo mean chalata hai, aur sum of x squared, jo variance chalata hai. Aapko dono clean karne hain, sirf mean fix karna sabse common half-mark loss hai.

Ek variation dhyan mein rakho. Agar value replace hone ke bajaye poori tarah omit hui thi, toh aap sirf minus w aur minus w squared girate ho, aur n ko ek se kam karte ho, kyunki ek observation kam hai.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Analysis & reverse problems: the formula toolkit

board_events.text: Subtopic 03 formula toolkit

board_events.latex: \sum x_{\text{corr}} = \sum x_{\text{wrong}} - w + c,\quad \sum x^2_{\text{corr}} = \sum x^2_{\text{wrong}} - w^2 + c^2

board_events.text: Same mean? Skip C.V. — compare σ. Corrected σ² must stay ≥ 0. C.V. is dimensionless.

segments.text: Here's the compact toolkit for this subtopic, gathered in one place for quick recall. I'm restating the tools, not re-teaching them.

At the top, the coefficient of variation is sigma over x bar times one hundred, valid whenever the mean isn't zero. And its reverse form recovers the mean: x bar equals sigma over the coefficient of variation, times one hundred.
The two master totals, the engine of every reverse problem: the sum of x i equals n times x bar, and the sum of x i squared equals n times the quantity sigma squared plus x bar squared.
For a correction, repair both totals: the corrected sum of x is the wrong sum minus w plus c, and the corrected sum of x squared is the wrong sum of squares minus w squared plus c squared.

For two missing observations, use the identity p plus q all squared equals p squared plus q squared plus two p q to get the product, then solve the quadratic t squared minus the sum times t, plus the product, equals zero.

And the combined-group formulas carried over from before: the combined mean is the frequency-weighted average of the two means, and the combined variance adds each group's own variance and its squared mean-gap, weighted by size.

Finally, three quick guardrails in red: if the means are equal, skip the coefficient of variation and just compare sigma; a corrected variance must stay at least zero; and the coefficient of variation is always dimensionless.
Yahaan is subtopic ke liye compact toolkit hai, quick recall ke liye ek jagah jama. Main tools restate kar raha hoon, dobara nahi padha raha.

Sabse upar, coefficient of variation sigma over x bar times one hundred hai, valid jab bhi mean zero na ho. Aur iska reverse form mean recover karta hai: x bar equals sigma over the coefficient of variation, times one hundred.
Do master totals, har reverse problem ka engine: sum of x i equals n times x bar, aur sum of x i squared equals n times the quantity sigma squared plus x bar squared.
Ek correction ke liye, dono totals repair karo: corrected sum of x wrong sum minus w plus c hai, aur corrected sum of x squared wrong sum of squares minus w squared plus c squared hai.

Do missing observations ke liye, identity p plus q poora squared equals p squared plus q squared plus two p q use karke product nikaalo, phir quadratic solve karo t squared minus the sum times t, plus the product, equals zero.

Aur pehle se aaye combined-group formulas: combined mean do means ka frequency-weighted average hai, aur combined variance har group ka apna variance aur uska squared mean-gap jodta hai, size se weighted.

Aakhir mein, teen quick guardrails red mein: agar means barabar hon, coefficient of variation skip karo aur bas sigma compare karo; ek corrected variance kam se kam zero rehna chahiye; aur coefficient of variation hamesha dimensionless hai.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Worked example: consistency vs. performance (two batsmen)

board_events.text: CBSE level: who is more consistent?
Arjun: mean 50 runs, SD 10.  Vikram: mean 40 runs, SD 6.  Different means → use C.V.
Lower C.V. → Vikram is the more consistent scorer.
But Arjun's higher average (50 vs 40) makes him the better bet to chase a steep total.
“Consistent” and “best” are different questions — this split verdict is exactly what examiners test.

segments.text: A perfect CBSE example to show that the coefficient of variation answers one question, but not every question. Batsman Arjun averages fifty runs with a standard deviation of ten. Batsman Vikram averages forty runs with a standard deviation of six. Who is more consistent, and who would you pick to chase a steep total?
The means differ, fifty versus forty, so standard deviation alone can't referee. We go straight to the coefficient of variation for each.
Arjun's coefficient of variation is ten over fifty, times one hundred, which is twenty percent.
Vikram's is six over forty, times one hundred, which is fifteen percent. Lower, so far so good.
Since fifteen percent is lower than twenty percent, Vikram is the more consistent scorer. If the question stopped at consistency, Vikram wins outright.
But consistency isn't everything. Arjun's higher average, fifty versus forty, makes him the better bet to chase a steep total, where raw run-scoring power matters more than steadiness.
That split verdict is exactly what examiners love to test. Consistent and best are two different questions, so read carefully which one is being asked before you commit your answer.

Ek perfect CBSE example ye dikhaane ke liye ki coefficient of variation ek sawaal answer karta hai, par har sawaal nahi. Batsman Arjun fifty runs average karta hai standard deviation ten ke saath. Batsman Vikram forty runs average karta hai standard deviation six ke saath. Kaun zyada consistent hai, aur ek steep total chase karne ke liye aap kise chunoge?
Means alag hain, fifty versus forty, toh standard deviation akela referee nahi kar sakta. Hum har ek ke liye seedhe coefficient of variation pe jaate hain.
Arjun ka coefficient of variation ten over fifty hai, times one hundred, jo twenty percent hai.
Vikram ka six over forty hai, times one hundred, jo fifteen percent hai. Kam, ab tak theek.
Kyunki fifteen percent twenty percent se kam hai, Vikram zyada consistent scorer hai. Agar sawaal consistency pe ruk jaata, Vikram outright jeet jaata.

Lekin consistency hi sab kuch nahi hai. Arjun ka zyada average, fifty versus forty, use ek steep total chase karne ke liye better bet banata hai, jahaan raw run-scoring power steadiness se zyada matter karti hai.
Wo split verdict theek wahi hai jo examiners test karna pasand karte hain. Consistent aur best do alag sawaal hain, toh apna answer commit karne se pehle dhyan se padho ki kaunsa poochha ja raha hai.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Worked example: reconstructing two missing observations

board_events.text: JEE Main: mean 6, variance 6.8, three of five known
Five observations, mean 6, variance 6.8; three are 2, 4, 9. Find the other two, a and b.

segments.text: Now the reverse machinery in action, a favourite JEE Main problem. The mean of five observations is six and their variance is six point eight. Three of them are two, four, and nine. Find the other two, call them a and b.
Read it as two unknowns, a and b, constrained by the mean and the variance. That's exactly the two equations we need.
First equation, from the mean. The five values must sum to five times six, which is thirty. So two plus four plus nine plus a plus b equals thirty, giving a plus b equals fifteen.

Second equation, from the variance. The sum of squared deviations about the mean six equals five times six point eight, which is thirty four. The three known values contribute sixteen plus four plus nine, so a minus six squared plus b minus six squared equals five.

Now substitute to make it clean. Let p be a minus six and q be b minus six. Then p plus q is fifteen minus twelve, which is three, and p squared plus q squared is five. Using the identity, three squared equals five plus two p q, so p q equals two.

With sum three and product two, p and q are the roots of t squared minus three t plus two equals zero, which factors to give t equals one and two. Undoing the substitution, a and b are seven and eight.

Always verify. The five observations two, four, nine, seven, eight have mean thirty over five, which is six, and variance sixteen plus four plus nine plus one plus four, over five, which is thirty four over five, exactly six point eight. Both boxes ticked.

Ab reverse machinery action mein, ek favourite JEE Main problem. Paanch observations ka mean six hai aur unka variance six point eight hai. Inme se teen hain two, four, aur nine. Baaki do nikaalo, inhe a aur b kehte hain.
Ise do unknowns ki tarah padho, a aur b, mean aur variance se constrained. Yahi wo do equations hain jo humein chahiye.
Pehla equation, mean se. Paanch values ka sum five times six hona chahiye, jo thirty hai. Toh two plus four plus nine plus a plus b equals thirty, jo deta hai a plus b equals fifteen.

Doosra equation, variance se. Mean six ke baare mein squared deviations ka sum five times six point eight hai, jo thirty four hai. Teen known values sixteen plus four plus nine contribute karte hain, toh a minus six squared plus b minus six squared equals five.

Ab substitute karke ise clean banao. p ko a minus six aur q ko b minus six maano. Toh p plus q fifteen minus twelve hai, jo three hai, aur p squared plus q squared five hai. Identity use karke, three squared equals five plus two p q, toh p q equals two.

Sum three aur product two ke saath, p aur q t squared minus three t plus two equals zero ke roots hain, jo factor hoke deta hai t equals one aur two. Substitution undo karke, a aur b seven aur eight hain.

Hamesha verify karo. Paanch observations two, four, nine, seven, eight ka mean thirty over five hai, jo six hai, aur variance sixteen plus four plus nine plus one plus four, over five, jo thirty four over five hai, exactly six point eight. Dono boxes ticked.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Worked example: correcting a misrecorded observation

board_events.text: JEE Main: an observation of 50 should have been 30
20 observations, mean 30, SD 5. A value recorded as 50 is actually 30. Correct the mean and SD.
One 4-σ outlier was doing almost all the work — repairing it collapses the SD from 5 to 2.

segments.text: This example shows exactly why you must repair both totals in a correction problem. For twenty observations, the mean and standard deviation were found to be thirty and five. On rechecking, a value recorded as fifty is actually thirty. Find the corrected mean and standard deviation.
The plan: recover the two wrong totals, repair each one, then recompute. Watch how the sum of squares does its own separate repair.

First the wrong totals. The wrong sum of x is twenty times thirty, which is six hundred. The wrong sum of x squared is twenty times the quantity five squared plus thirty squared, that's twenty times nine hundred twenty five, equals eighteen thousand five hundred.

Repair the sum of x: subtract the wrong fifty and add the correct thirty. Six hundred minus fifty plus thirty is five hundred eighty, so the corrected mean is five hundred eighty over twenty, which is twenty nine.

Repair the sum of squares the same way, but with squares: eighteen thousand five hundred, minus fifty squared, plus thirty squared. That's minus two thousand five hundred plus nine hundred, giving sixteen thousand nine hundred.

Now the corrected variance: sixteen thousand nine hundred over twenty, minus twenty nine squared. That's eight hundred forty five minus eight hundred forty one, equals four, so the corrected standard deviation is two.

Notice how dramatic that is: a single value that was four standard deviations out was doing almost all the work. Repairing that one outlier collapses the standard deviation from five all the way down to two.

Ye example theek dikhaata hai ki correction problem mein aapko dono totals kyun repair karne hain. Twenty observations ke liye, mean aur standard deviation thirty aur five nikle the. Rechecking pe, fifty record ki gayi ek value actually thirty hai. Corrected mean aur standard deviation nikaalo.
Plan: do wrong totals recover karo, har ek repair karo, phir dobara compute karo. Dekho sum of squares apni alag repair kaise karta hai.

Pehle wrong totals. Wrong sum of x twenty times thirty hai, jo six hundred hai. Wrong sum of x squared twenty times the quantity five squared plus thirty squared hai, yaani twenty times nine hundred twenty five, equals eighteen thousand five hundred.

Sum of x repair karo: wrong fifty ghatao aur correct thirty jodo. Six hundred minus fifty plus thirty five hundred eighty hai, toh corrected mean five hundred eighty over twenty hai, jo twenty nine hai.

Sum of squares usi tarah repair karo, par squares ke saath: eighteen thousand five hundred, minus fifty squared, plus thirty squared. Ye hai minus two thousand five hundred plus nine hundred, jo deta hai sixteen thousand nine hundred.

Ab corrected variance: sixteen thousand nine hundred over twenty, minus twenty nine squared. Ye hai eight hundred forty five minus eight hundred forty one, equals four, toh corrected standard deviation two hai.

Dekho ye kitna dramatic hai: ek akeli value jo four standard deviations bahar thi, lagbhag saara kaam kar rahi thi. Us ek outlier ko repair karna standard deviation ko five se seedhe do tak gira deta hai.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Worked example: combine two groups, then judge consistency

board_events.text: JEE Advanced: pool 100 students, then find C.V.
Group I: 40 students, mean 60, SD 8.  Group II: 60 students, mean 50, SD 6.
Group-mean deviations from 54: d₁ = 60 − 54 = 6, d₂ = 50 − 54 = −4.
Combined σ (8.44) exceeds both group SDs — the d² terms inject the between-group spread.

segments.text: The finale worked example fuses two chapter skills, combining groups and then judging consistency. Group one has forty students with mean sixty and standard deviation eight. Group two has sixty students with mean fifty and standard deviation six. Pooling all one hundred students, find the combined standard deviation and the combined coefficient of variation.
It's a two-stage problem: first combine to get the pooled variance, then normalise to get the coefficient of variation. Take them in order.
First the combined mean. It's forty times sixty plus sixty times fifty, all over one hundred. That's five thousand four hundred over one hundred, equals fifty four.
Now the group-mean deviations from that combined mean. d one is sixty minus fifty four, equals six. d two is fifty minus fifty four, equals minus four. These carry the between-group spread.

Apply the combined-variance formula. Each group contributes its variance plus its d squared, weighted by size: forty times sixty four plus thirty six, plus sixty times thirty six plus sixteen, all over one hundred. That's four thousand plus three thousand one hundred twenty, over one hundred, equals seventy one point two.

So the combined standard deviation is the square root of seventy one point two, about eight point four four. And the combined coefficient of variation is eight point four four over fifty four, times one hundred, roughly fifteen point six percent.

Note the same lesson as before, now with different numbers: the combined standard deviation, eight point four four, exceeds both group standard deviations, eight and six. Pooling groups with different means injects extra spread through the d squared terms, which a careless average-the-SDs approach would completely miss.

Finale worked example do chapter skills ko jodta hai, groups combine karna aur phir consistency judge karna. Group one mein forty students, mean sixty, standard deviation eight. Group two mein sixty students, mean fifty, standard deviation six. Saare one hundred students ko pool karke, combined standard deviation aur combined coefficient of variation nikaalo.
Ye ek two-stage problem hai: pehle combine karke pooled variance nikaalo, phir normalise karke coefficient of variation. Inhe kram se lo.
Pehle combined mean. Ye forty times sixty plus sixty times fifty hai, poora over one hundred. Ye hai five thousand four hundred over one hundred, equals fifty four.
Ab us combined mean se group-mean deviations. d one sixty minus fifty four hai, equals six. d two fifty minus fifty four hai, equals minus four. Ye between-group spread le ke chalte hain.

Combined-variance formula apply karo. Har group apna variance plus apna d squared contribute karta hai, size se weighted: forty times sixty four plus thirty six, plus sixty times thirty six plus sixteen, poora over one hundred. Ye hai four thousand plus three thousand one hundred twenty, over one hundred, equals seventy one point two.

Toh combined standard deviation seventy one point two ka square root hai, lagbhag eight point four four. Aur combined coefficient of variation eight point four four over fifty four hai, times one hundred, lagbhag fifteen point six percent.

Wahi lesson note karo jo pehle tha, ab alag numbers ke saath: combined standard deviation, eight point four four, dono group standard deviations se zyada hai, eight aur six. Alag means wale groups ko pool karna d squared terms ke through extra spread inject karta hai, jise ek careless average-the-SDs approach poori tarah miss kar deti.

sections.subtopic: Analysis of Frequency Distributions & Advanced Problem Types
sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: the reverse-problem traps

board_events.text: Four slips that quietly cost marks
1. Comparing different-mean series by σ instead of C.V. — a larger σ isn't “more variable” if the means differ.
2. Forgetting to repair ∑x_i² in correction problems — fixing only the mean is the #1 half-mark loss.
3. Feeding VARIANCE into the C.V. formula — C.V. uses the SD; using σ² inflates the answer enormously.
4. Reading “more consistent” as “better” — lower C.V. means steadier, not superior.
Reverse problems = bookkeeping on these two totals. Sanity: corrected σ² ≥ 0; a unit-carrying “C.V.” means you divided by the wrong thing.

segments.text: Let's close the subtopic, and the chapter's teaching, with the four traps that quietly drain marks on these analysis problems.

Slip one: comparing series with different means by their standard deviations instead of the coefficient of variation. A larger sigma does not make a series more variable if the means differ. Only when the means are equal may you compare sigma directly.

Slip two: forgetting to repair the sum of x squared in a correction problem. A wrong observation corrupts both the mean, through the sum of x, and the variance, through the sum of x squared. Fixing only the mean is the single most common half-mark loss.

Slip three: feeding the variance into the coefficient of variation formula. The coefficient of variation uses the standard deviation, not the variance. Slip in sigma squared and your answer inflates enormously.
Slip four: reading more consistent as better. A lower coefficient of variation means steadier, not superior. Always answer the exact question, consistency and performance are different verdicts.

Keep the two master totals in front of you: the sum of x i equals n x bar, and the sum of x i squared equals n times sigma squared plus x bar squared. Every reverse problem is just bookkeeping on these two numbers.

Two final sanity checks. A corrected variance must stay at least zero, if it goes negative you've mishandled the sum of squares. And recall the coefficient of variation is dimensionless, so if your answer carries units, you divided by the wrong thing.
Chalo subtopic, aur chapter ki teaching, ko un chaar traps ke saath band karte hain jo in analysis problems pe chupke se marks kha jaate hain.

Slip one: alag means wali series ko standard deviations se compare karna coefficient of variation ke bajaye. Badi sigma ek series ko zyada variable nahi banaati agar means alag hon. Sirf jab means barabar hon tabhi aap sigma seedhe compare kar sakte ho.

Slip two: correction problem mein sum of x squared repair karna bhoolna. Ek wrong observation dono ko corrupt karti hai, mean, sum of x ke through, aur variance, sum of x squared ke through. Sirf mean fix karna sabse common half-mark loss hai.

Slip three: variance ko coefficient of variation formula mein daalna. Coefficient of variation standard deviation use karta hai, variance nahi. sigma squared daalo aur aapka answer enormously inflate ho jaata hai.
Slip four: zyada consistent ko better padhna. Kam coefficient of variation matlab steadier, superior nahi. Hamesha exact sawaal answer karo, consistency aur performance alag verdicts hain.
Do master totals apne saamne rakho: sum of x i equals n x bar, aur sum of x i squared equals n times sigma squared plus x bar squared. Har reverse problem in do numbers pe bas bookkeeping hai.

Do aakhri sanity checks. Ek corrected variance kam se kam zero rehna chahiye, agar negative jaaye toh aapne sum of squares galat handle kiya. Aur yaad rakho coefficient of variation dimensionless hai, toh agar aapka answer units rakhta hai, aapne galat cheez se divide kiya.

board_events.text: Statistics — every formula, all three subtopics
Sanity, always: M.D. ≤ Range, σ² ≥ 0, σ ≤ Range, C.V. dimensionless.

segments.text: Here is the whole chapter's toolkit on a single board. This is a recap, so I'm restating every formula for fast recall, not deriving anything again, treat it as your one-glance reference before an exam.
From dispersion basics: the range is x max minus x min, and the coefficient of range is that difference over the sum of the extremes.
Mean deviation about any central value a is one over n sum of the absolute deviations, or one over N sum of f i times them for frequency data, and remember it is least about the median.
Variance, in both the shortcut and the frequency form: one over n sum of x i squared minus x bar squared, or its weighted version. And standard deviation is always the positive square root.
For grouped data by coding, variance is h squared times the bracket of sum f i d i squared over N, minus the square of sum f i d i over N, with d i the step deviation.

The comparison and transformation tools: the coefficient of variation is sigma over x bar times one hundred; and under x maps to a x plus b, range, mean deviation, and standard deviation all scale by the absolute value of a, while variance scales by a squared.

And the advanced results: combined variance from the group means and variances; the variance of the first n natural numbers is n squared minus one over twelve; and the two reverse-problem totals, sum of x i and sum of x i squared.

Your permanent guardrails, in red: mean deviation is at most the range, variance is non-negative, sigma is at most the range, and the coefficient of variation is dimensionless. Check these on every answer.

Yahaan poore chapter ka toolkit ek single board pe hai. Ye ek recap hai, toh main fast recall ke liye har formula restate kar raha hoon, dobara kuch derive nahi kar raha, ise exam se pehle apni one-glance reference samjho.
Dispersion basics se: range x max minus x min hai, aur coefficient of range wo difference extremes ke sum se hai.

Kisi bhi central value a ke baare mein mean deviation one over n sum of the absolute deviations hai, ya frequency data ke liye one over N sum of f i times them, aur yaad rakho ye median ke baare mein sabse kam hai.
Variance, dono shortcut aur frequency form mein: one over n sum of x i squared minus x bar squared, ya iska weighted version. Aur standard deviation hamesha positive square root hai.
Coding se grouped data ke liye, variance h squared times the bracket of sum f i d i squared over N hai, minus square of sum f i d i over N, d i step deviation ke saath.

Comparison aur transformation tools: coefficient of variation sigma over x bar times one hundred hai; aur x maps to a x plus b ke under, range, mean deviation, aur standard deviation sab absolute value of a se scale hote hain, jabki variance a squared se.

Aur advanced results: group means aur variances se combined variance; first n natural numbers ka variance n squared minus one over twelve hai; aur do reverse-problem totals, sum of x i aur sum of x i squared.

Aapke permanent guardrails, red mein: mean deviation zyada se zyada range hai, variance non-negative hai, sigma zyada se zyada range hai, aur coefficient of variation dimensionless hai. Har answer pe ye check karo.

board_events.text: Median Minimises Mean-deviation (3 M's). The MEAN minimises mean-square deviation.
Frequency tables: the divisor is ALWAYS N = ∑f_i — never the number of rows/classes.
Transformation “Add doesn't matter, Multiply scales”: |a| for Range/M.D./SD, a² for variance.
Consistency: lower C.V. wins. Same mean? Skip C.V. and just compare σ.
Reverse: ∑x=nx̄, ∑x²=n(σ²+x̄²); correct with −w+c and −w²+c². Sanity: M.D.≤Range, σ²≥0, σ≤Range.

segments.text: Last board of the chapter, the rapid-recall cheat sheet. Everything here is a memory hook, glance at it the night before and again in the last five minutes.

First, the big picture as a ladder. Dispersion measures refine from crude to sophisticated: range, then mean deviation, then variance, then standard deviation, each fixing a weakness of the one before.

The two minimisation crowns, in red: the median minimises mean deviation, remember the three M's, Median Minimises Mean-deviation. And the mean minimises mean-square deviation, which is why variance sits on the mean.
For any frequency table, the divisor is always N, the total frequency, the sum of the f i. Never divide by the number of rows or classes, that's the number-one marks-loser in this chapter.

The transformation mnemonic: Add doesn't matter, Multiply scales. Range, mean deviation, and standard deviation each scale by the absolute value of a, while variance scales by a squared, and the additive constant does nothing.

For consistency, lower coefficient of variation always wins. And a time-saver: if the two means are equal, skip the coefficient of variation entirely and just compare the standard deviations, they give the same ranking.

Finally the reverse-problem kit, in red: the sum of x is n x bar, the sum of x squared is n times sigma squared plus x bar squared; to correct a value, add minus w plus c to the first total and minus w squared plus c squared to the second. And the sanity trio you should never skip: mean deviation at most the range, variance never negative, and standard deviation at most the range.
Chapter ka aakhri board, rapid-recall cheat sheet. Yahaan sab kuch ek memory hook hai, ise raat pehle dekho aur phir aakhri paanch minute mein.

Pehle, big picture ek ladder ki tarah. Dispersion measures crude se sophisticated tak refine hote hain: range, phir mean deviation, phir variance, phir standard deviation, har ek pehle wale ki ek weakness theek karta hua.

Do minimisation crowns, red mein: median mean deviation ko minimise karta hai, teen M's yaad rakho, Median Minimises Mean-deviation. Aur mean mean-square deviation ko minimise karta hai, isiliye variance mean pe baithta hai.
Kisi bhi frequency table ke liye, divisor hamesha N hai, total frequency, f i ka sum. Kabhi rows ya classes ki number se divide mat karo, ye is chapter ka number-one marks-loser hai.

Transformation mnemonic: Add doesn't matter, Multiply scales. Range, mean deviation, aur standard deviation har ek absolute value of a se scale hote hain, jabki variance a squared se, aur additive constant kuch nahi karta.

Consistency ke liye, kam coefficient of variation hamesha jeetta hai. Aur ek time-saver: agar do means barabar hain, coefficient of variation poori tarah skip karo aur bas standard deviations compare karo, wo same ranking dete hain.

Aakhir mein reverse-problem kit, red mein: sum of x n x bar hai, sum of x squared n times sigma squared plus x bar squared hai; ek value correct karne ke liye, pehle total mein minus w plus c jodo aur doosre mein minus w squared plus c squared. Aur wo sanity trio jise kabhi skip mat karna: mean deviation zyada se zyada range, variance kabhi negative nahi, aur standard deviation zyada se zyada range.
